question: What mathematical structure remains in incorrect transformer solutions to small linear-algebra problems, can simple invariants predict those failures, and how does the training matrix distribution affect out-of-distribution generalization?

key_findings.claim: A diagonalization transformer preserves several solution invariants even when its complete prediction fails.
key_findings.evidence: On 50,000 random 5-by-5 matrices, full diagonalization accuracy is 92.0%, while eigenvalues are within 1% in 99.9% of cases and every predicted row and column has norm in [0.99,1.01] in 98.9%; similar gaps persist for a half-trained model and 6-by-6 matrices.

key_findings.claim: Problem-specific numerical invariants accurately flag most failures in the tested distributions.
key_findings.evidence: A threshold on the predicted eigenvector matrix's condition number classifies diagonalization successes and failures with 99.3% accuracy; an input-matrix condition-number threshold predicts inversion success in 98.0% of cases.

key_findings.claim: Training on unbounded symmetric eigenvalue distributions produces striking cross-distribution transfer on the enumerated matrix ensembles.
key_findings.evidence: For 5-by-5 eigenvalues, Gaussian and Laplace-trained models score essentially 100% across seven test ensembles, whereas semicircle training transfers poorly; the advantage grows for 8-by-8 and 10-by-10 problems and reduces examples needed to reach target accuracy.

key_findings.claim: The results refute a universal 'mere interpolation' description only within a narrow operational sense.
key_findings.evidence: Positive-definite test matrices have negligible direct overlap with symmetric-distribution training examples, so nearest-example memorization is implausible; however, the experiments do not identify the learned algorithm or rule out interpolation in a representation induced by the network.

key_findings.claim: Calling preserved output constraints 'deep mathematical properties' does not establish mechanistic interpretability.
key_findings.evidence: The paper measures external behavior—eigenvalue error, vector norms, orthogonality, and condition numbers—but does not analyze activations, attention, causal components, or internal computation.

key_findings.claim: The verifier result is partly circular and distribution-calibrated.
key_findings.evidence: The task's official success criterion already checks the same algebraic residuals, while the proposed thresholds are selected and evaluated on one synthetic distribution without prospective calibration, coverage-risk curves, or comparison to model confidence.

method.core_idea: Train sequence-to-sequence transformers on serialized matrices and solutions, then decompose binary task accuracy into mathematically meaningful residuals and sweep random-matrix generators to expose failure structure and distribution transfer.
method.mechanism: Evaluate eigenvalue error, unit norms, pairwise orthogonality, condition numbers, and inverse residuals; train separate models on semicircle, uniform, Gaussian, Laplace, positive, and Marchenko-Pastur ensembles; compare every training-test distribution pair.
assumptions: Small fixed-dimensional synthetic matrices reveal relevant properties of mathematical transformers.
Quantized sequence encodings do not dominate the observed failures.
Chosen random-matrix ensembles constitute meaningful out-of-domain shifts.
Condition-number thresholds calibrated on the same distribution will transfer.
External invariant satisfaction is evidence about learned mathematical concepts rather than an output-format shortcut.

techniques.role: Checks partial mathematical correctness underneath a binary residual threshold.
Predicts ill-conditioned outputs or inputs likely to violate the task tolerance.
Controls eigenvalue support, sign, tails, and conditioning across train and test.
Learns matrix-to-solution mappings from cross-entropy on numeric tokens.

evaluations.metric: Residual accuracy, eigenvalue relative error, vector norm, orthogonality, and output condition number.
evaluations.result: 92.0% complete accuracy coexists with near-universal accurate eigenvalues and unit norms; output conditioning flags most failures.
evaluations.baseline: The same audits on half-trained and 6-by-6 lower-accuracy models.

evaluations.metric: Product-to-identity residual, direct inverse error, and input condition number.
evaluations.result: Official accuracy is 89.0%, but 98.2% of predictions are within 5% of the numeric inverse; an input condition threshold predicts 98.0% of outcomes.
evaluations.baseline: Task success threshold versus a direct numerical-distance criterion.

evaluations.setting: Eigenvalue prediction for 5-, 8-, and 10-dimensional matrices across seven ensembles.
evaluations.metric: Exact-with-tolerance accuracy and examples to reach 99%.
evaluations.result: Gaussian and especially Laplace training transfer broadly and learn faster than compact-support training.
evaluations.baseline: Models trained separately on each test generator.

evaluations.setting: 5-by-5 diagonalization and symmetric inversion across generator shifts.
evaluations.metric: Task accuracy matrix and learning samples.
evaluations.result: The broad-transfer trend largely persists, although inversion invalidates a simple 'more condition-number edge cases' explanation.
evaluations.baseline: Seven training distributions including positive-only ensembles.

limitations: The paper studies three tasks, small fixed matrix sizes, synthetic distributions, and one transformer family.
Reviewer inference: behavioral invariant tests are not an internal or causal explanation of computation.
Reviewer inference: no non-transformer numerical approximator or classical algorithm-learning baseline establishes architectural specificity.
Reviewer inference: threshold verifiers are evaluated in-sample and are not assessed for calibration under the very distribution shifts studied.
Reviewer inference: full task verification is already cheap for these linear-algebra problems, limiting practical value.
Reviewer inference: high accuracy on a disjoint support does not distinguish a learned algorithm from smooth function approximation.
failure_modes: Numeric tokenization produces rounding patterns that mimic structural understanding.
Condition thresholds fail after dimension, precision, or eigenvalue distribution changes.
Repeated or nearly repeated eigenvalues make eigenvectors non-identifiable up to a larger rotation group.
The model satisfies norms and eigenvalues but pairs eigenvectors incorrectly.
A broad training generator overweights extreme values and degrades precision in a deployment-specific narrow range.
Sequence length growth breaks a method that works only at trained matrix sizes.
reusable_insights: Exact-match or residual accuracy should be decomposed into domain invariants before labeling mathematical outputs hallucinations.
Input-only difficulty predictors can support selective prediction, but must be evaluated with risk-coverage curves under shift.
Training-distribution support and tails can matter more for algorithmic transfer than matching the expected test distribution.
A failed intuitive explanation—here, exposure to high condition numbers—should be reported alongside the surviving empirical pattern.
open_questions: What internal circuit computes eigenvalues and normalizes vectors, and is it causally reused across dimensions?
Do invariant-based verifiers calibrate on unseen dimensions, precision formats, and nonsymmetric matrices?
Which property of Gaussian and Laplace generators, if not merely edge-case conditioning, causes broad transfer?
Can curricula over generator mixtures reduce data further while retaining worst-case numerical stability?
How do these models compare with recurrent, graph, or neural-operator architectures under length extrapolation?

competitive_landscape.title: Linear algebra with transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Charton's earlier paper establishes nine numerical tasks and the encoding schemes; the reviewed note reuses that setup to analyze partial correctness, failure prediction, and generator-dependent transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Symbolic Brittleness in Sequence Models: On Systematic Generalization in Symbolic Mathematics
competitive_landscape.difference: Welleck et al. use perturbations and genetic search to uncover local, compositional, and OOD failures in symbolic integration, tempering broad conclusions from successful random-matrix shifts.

competitive_landscape.title: A Symbolic Framework for Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning and Generalisation with Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Meadows et al. perturb operators, symmetries, and surface forms in derivations and report drops up to 80 F1 points; the reviewed paper varies matrix spectra but not reasoning-form perturbations.

competitive_landscape.title: What Algorithms can Transformers Learn? A Study in Length Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: This work links length generalization to short RASP programs and changes scratchpad form to test the conjecture; Charton's behavioral invariants do not specify an internal algorithm or test length systematically.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: McLeish et al. isolate digit position encoding and reach 20-to-100-digit extrapolation, showing an architectural route to numeric OOD generalization beyond training-generator selection.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Math-transformer errors remain roughly right, admit simple mathematical predictors, and can generalize far outside the training distribution when the generator is chosen well.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Large synthetic test sets reveal preserved invariants, accurate condition-number classifiers, and broad cross-ensemble transfer for Gaussian and Laplace training.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The fine-grained error audit and generator matrix are informative, but 'interpretability,' 'hallucination,' and 'not interpolation' are stronger labels than the behavioral evidence warrants. Later systematic and length-generalization work supplies more discriminating tests.

reviewer_notes: Read all eight extracted pages, including generator definitions and additional inversion/generalization tables. Closest and subsequent papers were checked at primary arXiv, AAAI, ACL, and OpenReview records on 2026-08-23.
